name: Northland

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Syrah, Riesling and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay, Syrah and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Pinot Gris is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium. Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. It is very acid, which locks up nutrients, so growers spread lime to raise the pH.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
